translationRepairs: His father, Shouyu, served as legal adviser to the Zhengzhou defense command.
His father, Shouyu, served as administrative assistant to the Zhengzhou defense commissioner.
防禦判官 is an administrative assistant, not legal adviser.
In 933 he passed the jinshi examination, served as staff officer to the Zhongwu commissioner, and was later appointed magistrate of Fengqiu.
In 933 he passed the jinshi examination, served as judge on the staff of the Zhongwu military governor, and was later appointed magistrate of Fengqiu.
節度推官 is a judicial staff post under a military governor.
In the summer of his sixth year on the throne, Shizong marched north while Zhi, ill, stayed in the capital and was given a million cash to buy medicine.
In the summer of the sixth year of Xiande (959), Shizong marched north while Zhi, ill, stayed in the capital and was given a million cash to buy medicine.
六年 continues the Xiande era, not a regnal year of Shizong.
When Emperor Gong succeeded, Zhi was made Grand Preceptor with third-rank opening privileges and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
When Emperor Gong succeeded, Zhi was made Commander Unequalled in Honor and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
開府儀同三司 is the Commander Unequalled in Honor title.
Your younger brother Guangyi, military commissioner of Taining, has shown command talent since taking military office and has won wide respect in his regional post;
Your younger brother Guangyi, military governor of Taining, has shown command talent since taking military office and has won wide respect in his regional post;

Lu Yuqing, academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, and Zhao Pu, deputy military affairs commissioner, are deeply versed in governance, long tested in the founding lord's service, and plainly loyal.

Lü Yuqing, academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, and Zhao Pu, deputy military affairs commissioner, are deeply versed in governance, long tested in the founding lord's service, and plainly loyal.
呂 romanizes as Lü with umlaut.
After the army returned he was made Attendant Within.
After the army returned he was made Supervising Secretary.
He died in the sixth year at the age of forty-six.
He died in the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo (981) at the age of forty-six.
Era context clarified for 六年.
Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he became a compiler and was assigned to the Historiography Institute, later serving as Right Remembrancer and Left Supplementation Censor.
Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he became a compiler and was assigned to the Historiography Institute, later serving as Right Remembrancer and Left Rectifier of Omissions.
左補闕 is Left Rectifier of Omissions.
His maternal uncle Xi was miserly by nature. A former vice intendant of Xingyuan, he lived in the capital region and had amassed a fortune of tens of thousands.
His elder brother Xi, born of the same mother was miserly by nature. A former vice intendant of Xingyuan, he lived in the capital region and had amassed a fortune of tens of thousands.
母兄 is an elder full brother; 116 calls him 兄.
A relative arriving from Chang'an deceived him, saying, "Your uncle no longer hoards his wealth—he has been spending gold without limit."
A relative arriving from Chang'an deceived him, saying, "The vice intendant no longer hoards his wealth—he has been spending gold without limit."
少尹 refers to Xi by office, not uncle.

At that time Song Bai had been demoted from the Hanlin Academy, while Jia Huangzhong and Li Hang served as participants in government and Su Yijian had become chief academician. Gao repeatedly wrote to the chief minister's office seeking a Hanlin post and told Li Fang, "My late uncle once gave me a volume of edict drafts and said my talent suited this office."

At that time Song Bai of the Hanlin Academy had been demoted to Fuzhou, while Jia Huangzhong and Li Hang served as participants in government and Su Yijian had become chief academician. Gao repeatedly wrote to the chief minister's office seeking a Hanlin post and told Li Fang, "My late uncle once gave me a volume of edict drafts and said my talent suited this office."
左遷鄜州 names the place of demotion.
During the Qianyou era of Later Han, Pu passed the jinshi examination in the top class and became a Secretariat gentleman.
During the Qianyou era of Later Han, Pu passed the jinshi examination in the top class and became a gentleman of the Palace Library.
秘書郎 belongs to the Palace Library.
When Li Shouzhen held Hezhong, Zhao Sijian rebelled in the capital region, and Wang Jingchong rebelled in Fengxiang, Guo Wei marched to suppress them and recruited Pu to his staff.
When Li Shouzhen held Hezhong, Zhao Siwan rebelled in the capital region, and Wang Jingchong rebelled in Fengxiang, Guo Wei marched to suppress them and recruited Pu to his staff.
綰 is read wan; the name is Zhao Siwan.
In the summer of the sixth year he was made a participant in military affairs.
In the summer of the sixth year of Xiande (959) he was made a participant in military affairs.
Era context for 六年 clarified.
He died in the eighth month of the seventh year at the age of sixty-one.
He died in the eighth month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo (982) at the age of sixty-one.
Era context for 七年 clarified.
Yizheng's son Keming married Princess Zheng, Taizong's daughter, changed his name to Yiyong, and was granted to share his father's posthumous honors—see the Biography of Imperial Affines.
Yizheng's son Keming married Princess Zheng, Taizong's daughter, changed his name to Yiyong, and was ordered to rank in the same generation as his father—see the Biography of Imperial Affines.
令與其父同行 concerns generational naming rank.

Later Han law forbade the export of ox hides to the capital, and many hides rotted in summer rains on the road. Zuo had armor patterns distributed to the prefectures so hides could be cut locally for delivery, which greatly eased the burden on the people.

Later Han law forbade private trade in ox hides, which had to be carted to the capital, and many hides rotted in summer rains on the road. Zuo had armor patterns distributed to the prefectures so hides could be cut locally for delivery, which greatly eased the burden on the people.
漢法禁牛革，輦送京師 rendering corrected.

Late in Qianyou, Emperor Yin plotted with Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye and others to execute chief ministers Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao. A secret edict ordered Chun commissioner Li Hongyi to kill cavalry general Wang Yin and directed Guo Chong to kill Guo Wei.

Late in Qianyou, Emperor Yin plotted with Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye and others to execute chief ministers Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao. A secret edict ordered Chanzhou commissioner Li Hongyi to kill cavalry general Wang Yin and directed Guo Chong to kill Guo Wei.
澶帥 is the commissioner of Chanzhou.
When Guo Wei took charge of military affairs, he asked Renpu how many troops were stationed below the passes. Renpu recited the figure from memory and wrote out sixty thousand men by hand.
When Guo Wei took charge of military affairs, he asked Renpu how many troops were stationed at the capital. Renpu recited the figure from memory and wrote out sixty thousand men by hand.
闕下 means at the capital.
On accession he made Renpu deputy privy council receptionist, then soon promoted him to General of the Right Forest Guard while keeping him as receptionist.
On accession he made Renpu Deputy Edict Transmitter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then soon promoted him to General of the Right Forest Guard while keeping him as Edict Transmitter.
樞密副承旨 rendered as an office title. 承旨 rendered consistently.
In the winter of 986, when the Khitans raided the border, the court ordered its sons-in-law to guard key posts: Wang Chengyan at Daming, Shi Baoji at Heyang, and Xianxin at Chunzhou.
In the winter of 986, when the Khitans raided the border, the court ordered its sons-in-law to guard key posts: Wang Chengyan at Daming, Shi Baoji at Heyang, and Xianxin at Chanzhou.
Early in the Jingde era he accompanied the court to Chunzhou, where Shi Baoji and Li Jilong served as array marshals.
Early in the Jingde era he accompanied the court to Chanzhou, where Shi Baoji and Li Jilong served as array marshals.
Before the Fenyin sacrifice he was put in charge of Chunzhou, and Palace Deputy Capital Gate Director Zhang Jineng was sent to convey the imperial instructions.
Before the Fenyin sacrifice he was put in charge of Chanzhou, and Deputy Director of the Palace Domestic Service Zhang Jineng was sent to convey the imperial instructions.
澶州 is read Chanzhou. 入內副都知 is a palace eunuch office.
In 993 the Yellow River burst at Chunyuan and flooded the north city. Xianxin was again put in charge of the prefecture.
In 993 the Yellow River burst at Chanyuan and flooded the north city. Xianxin was again put in charge of the prefecture.
Early in the Tianxi era he was made chief administrator of Shaanzhou and military commissioner of the Baoping army.
Early in the Tianxi era he was made chief administrator of Shanzhou and military commissioner of the Baoping army.
陜州 is Shanzhou in Henan.
In the fourth year an edict granted him one hundred thousand cash beyond his salary.
In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo (979) an edict granted him one hundred thousand cash beyond his salary.
In the fifth year he was fined one season's salary for sending a personal clerk to buy timber on the western frontier and falsely exempting transit taxes.
In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo (980) he was fined one season's salary for sending a personal clerk to buy timber on the western frontier and falsely exempting transit taxes.
In the fourth year the Yellow River ran clear in his jurisdiction. Xianxin reported the omen and received an edict of commendation.
In the fourth year of Yongxi (987) the Yellow River ran clear in his jurisdiction. Xianxin reported the omen and received an edict of commendation.

In the seventh year he petitioned for a new appointment. The emperor showed the memorial to Xiang Minzhong and said, "Xianxin is already an imperial in-law and a military commissioner—what more does he want?"

In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1014) he petitioned for a new appointment. The emperor showed the memorial to Xiang Minzhong and said, "Xianxin is already an imperial in-law and a military commissioner—what more does he want?"
In the second year he was made military commissioner of the Wucheng army and prefect of Caozhou.
In the second year of Jingde (1005) he was made military commissioner of the Wucheng army and prefect of Caozhou.
While Taizu was still heir apparent, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian visited Renpu's home and found the young Xianxin standing dutifully at his mother's side with the composure of a grown man.
While Taizu had not yet ascended the throne, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian visited Renpu's home and found the young Xianxin standing dutifully at his mother's side with the composure of a grown man.
潛邸 is the residence before accession.
He also proposed installing ceremonial stones in the inner hall and was made training commissioner of Enzhou.
He also proposed installing ceremonial stones in the inner hall and was made regimentation commissioner of Enzhou.
He died in the second year of the Tianxi era.
He died in the second year of the Tianxi era (1018).
In office Zhaoliang was obsessively watchful, often sending agents to spy on colleagues. Yin Derun, drafter in the Bureau of Military Affairs, despised him.
In office Zhaoliang was obsessively watchful, often sending agents to spy on colleagues. Yin Derun, Edict Transmitter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, despised him.
